overview: On May 30, 2024, the board appointed Hermenegildo Paulo as the new Director of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion for the district.

Board: The board approved the appointment of Hermenegildo Paulo.

Facilities Bond Referendum 2024.current_status: Following a successful referendum, the district is now actively implementing the funded facilities projects. Work is underway on security camera installation at Skillin Elementary, roofing at Small Elementary, and secure vestibules at several schools.
overview: On July 14, 2025, the district reported significant progress on summer facilities projects funded by the referendum, including camera, roofing, and vestibule installations.
On September 9, 2024, citizens voiced strong opposition to the artificial turf field component of the bond, citing environmental risks like microplastics and PFAS contamination.

On July 8, 2024, the Board voted to send three separate bond questions to the City Council for the November ballot: $3 million for security, $1 million for maintenance, and $12.2 million for the stadium complex, which included a synthetic turf field.

On June 10, 2024, the Board unanimously directed the administration to prepare formal proposals for three separate bond referendums covering safety, maintenance, and a high school stadium renovation, with a total cost not to exceed $17 million.

Board: Voted 6-1 to advance the stadium complex referendum after a contentious debate on July 8, 2024.
Unanimously approved sending the security and maintenance bond questions to the City Council on July 8, 2024.
Initially debated the environmental and safety aspects of artificial turf versus natural grass on June 10, 2024.
Administration: On July 8, 2024, Superintendent Matheney detailed three proposed bond referendums for the November ballot, specifying costs and materials for the stadium's synthetic turf field.
On June 10, 2024, the Superintendent proposed the projects and recommended a specific recyclable, organic-infill artificial turf product for the stadium.
Citizens: In September 2024, speakers raised environmental concerns about the proposed artificial turf, including microplastics, PFAS, and the heat island effect.
In July 2024, numerous parents and youth sports coaches spoke overwhelmingly in favor of the stadium renovation and synthetic turf, citing poor conditions and safety issues with the current field.

Equity in Resource Allocation.current_status: The board has approved a motion to provide additional resources to schools with higher percentages of economically disadvantaged students. A full report on this new allocation is expected by August 2024.
overview: On May 13, 2024, the board passed a motion to ensure schools with disproportionate percentages of economically disadvantaged students receive additional resources and staffing, with a full report on the allocation due by August 2024.

Board: Passed a motion to direct additional resources to schools with higher needs to support student learning.

Facilities Master Plan.current_status: The administration has identified key facility priorities, including security upgrades, deferred maintenance, and stadium renovations. A dedicated workshop is scheduled for May 30, 2024, to discuss these capital improvements in detail.
overview: On May 13, 2024, the administration outlined key facility priorities such as security upgrades, HVAC systems at Skillin, and stadium complex renovations, scheduling a workshop for further discussion.

Administration: Recommended focusing on security upgrades, deferred maintenance like HVAC at Skillin, and stadium renovations.

Student Activity Accessibility.current_status: The Board is exploring the costs of potential future positions that could enhance student accessibility, such as a Director of Intervention and Mental Health and an additional pre-K classroom, though these are currently unfunded.
overview: On March 28, 2024, the administration provided cost estimates for potential but unfunded positions aimed at improving student support and access, including a Director of Intervention and Mental Health and an additional pre-K classroom.

Board: Inquired about the costs of unfunded positions related to student support and pre-K.
Administration: Provided cost estimates for a Director of Intervention and Mental Health ($100,000) and an additional pre-K classroom ($175,000).

FY25 Budget.current_status: The Board of Education approved the final FY25 school budget articles, totaling over $69 million. The budget maintains essential services while navigating the loss of federal funds and rising costs.
overview: On May 13, 2024, the Board approved the final FY25 school budget articles, totaling over $69 million.
On April 8, 2024, the Board approved a revised budget that used savings from lower health insurance costs to add a new district-level Mental Health and Student Intervention position.
On March 28, 2024, the Board of Education unanimously approved the final FY25 Superintendent’s Budget, which included a 5% operating increase and a 3.82% mill rate increase.
On March 25, 2024, the administration announced that an art teacher position previously funded by COVID-era grants would be moved into the local budget.
On March 18, 2024, the administration presented the proposed $69.5 million budget, highlighting the fiscal challenge of losing $1.5 million in federal COVID-19 relief funds.
On March 11, 2024, the Superintendent presented the initial $69.4 million proposed budget, noting it did not fund requests for a mental health leadership position or an additional Pre-K section.

Board: During the April 8, 2024 meeting, some members debated whether funds for a new mental health position would be better spent expanding the Pre-K program.
On March 28, 2024, the Board inquired about the costs of several requested but unfunded positions, including a Director of Intervention and Mental Health and an additional pre-K classroom.
Members expressed strong support on March 25, 2024 for continuing the Extended Learning Opportunities (ELO) program and restoring the art teacher position.
On March 25, 2024, members DeAngelis and Ryan advocated for exploring a dedicated grant writer position to secure funding for programs.
Administration: On April 8, 2024, the Superintendent proposed using savings from lower-than-expected health insurance costs to add a new district-level Mental Health and Student Intervention position.
The Superintendent consistently highlighted the challenge of losing $1.5 million in federal COVID-19 funds, which had supported 19 positions.
On March 25, 2024, the administration committed to finding an alternative staffing and funding solution to continue the Extended Learning Opportunities (ELO) program.
The Superintendent presented the 5% operating budget increase as competitive and fair to taxpayers compared to neighboring districts.
Staff: During public comment on March 18, 2024, teachers advocated strongly against the proposed elimination of a high school art teacher position.
Citizens: On April 8, 2024, a parent suggested that investing in preventative measures like Pre-K could be a more proactive use of funds than creating a new mental health leadership role.
During the March 18, 2024 meeting, community members advocated against eliminating a high school art teacher position.
On March 11, 2024, some citizens expressed concern that the proposed budget increase might not be sufficient to meet the district's growing and complex needs.

Multi-Tiered Systems of Support.current_status: The district is actively implementing a Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS) for academic, behavioral, and social-emotional needs. Principals are using the new EDU climber platform to make data-driven decisions.
overview: On March 18, 2024, elementary and middle school principals presented on the implementation of MTSS, highlighting the use of the new EDU climber platform for data-driven decision-making.

Administration: Principals are implementing MTSS to address academic, behavioral, and social-emotional needs.
The administration is emphasizing a data-driven approach using the EDU climber platform.

School Calendar 2024-2025.current_status: The 2024-2025 school calendar has been approved by the board. A revision on March 28, 2024, extended the final day of school by one day to June 13, 2025.
overview: On March 28, 2024, the board unanimously approved a revision to the 2024-2025 school year calendar, extending the school year by one day to June 13, 2025.
The board had previously given its unanimous initial approval for the 2024-2025 school year calendar on March 11, 2024.

Board: Voted unanimously on March 28, 2024, to approve a revision extending the school year by one day.
Voted unanimously on March 11, 2024, to approve the initial 2024-2025 school calendar.

Homeless Student Services.current_status: The district's McKinney-Vento program is seeing a significant increase in students living in doubled-up situations, while a new pilot grant has shown success in preventing student homelessness.
overview: On March 18, 2024, an update on the McKinney-Vento program noted a doubling of students in doubled-up housing situations due to the housing crisis and highlighted the success of a new pilot grant aimed at preventing student homelessness.

Multilingual Programs.current_status: The Multilingual Department has presented a new master plan and is implementing new language access initiatives. This includes a new phone interpretation service to better support the district's diverse student population.
overview: On March 18, 2024, the Multilingual Department presented its new master plan and language access initiatives, which include a new inbound phone interpretation service.

Administration: Outlined a new master plan and language access initiatives, including a phone interpretation service.

DEI Coordinator Resignation.current_status: The board has formally addressed the resignation of DEI Coordinator Mohammed Albehadli, which was prompted by a racist incident. The district has reaffirmed its commitment to DEI work and is facing public calls for comprehensive action to address systemic inequities and improve staff diversity.
overview: On February 12, 2024, the board formally addressed the resignation, expressing sadness and anger while hearing public comment urging comprehensive action on systemic inequities and staff diversity.

On January 22, 2024, the Superintendent announced that DEI Director Mohammad Albehadli had resigned due to a vile, threatening email and pledged that the district's DEI work would continue with urgency.

Board: Members expressed sadness and anger over the racist incident that led to the resignation.
The board reaffirmed its commitment to DEI work.
Administration: Administrators urged the board to take thoughtful, comprehensive action to address systemic inequities and improve staff retention.
Superintendent Matheney praised Mr. Albehadli's service and pledged that the district's DEI work will continue with urgency.
Citizens: Public commenters urged the board to take comprehensive action, improve recruitment of diverse staff, and engage with the city on housing issues.
A student representative spoke about the personal impact of losing Mr. Albehadli as a role model.
Citizens expressed sadness over the departure and requested a greater focus on increasing staff diversity.

Physical Restraint and Seclusion Policy.current_status: The board has given final approval to the Physical Restraint and Seclusion Policy. This policy is now officially adopted by the district.
overview: On January 8, 2024, the board gave final approval to the policy concerning physical restraint and seclusion as part of a unanimous consent agenda vote.

Board: Unanimously approved the final policy as part of a consent agenda on January 8, 2024.

Transportation Challenges.current_status: The district is experiencing transportation staffing shortages. To help address the issue, the board has approved a new transportation logistics specialist position.
overview: On February 12, 2024, the Superintendent reported ongoing transportation staffing shortages, and the board approved a new transportation logistics specialist position to help address the issue.

Board: Approved a new job description for a transportation logistics specialist.
Administration: The Superintendent identified transportation staffing shortages as a key district challenge.

Student Mental Health.current_status: The Director of Mental/Behavioral Health position is currently under scrutiny during budget discussions. The Superintendent is defending the role as essential for providing specialized expertise, while some board members and citizens question its retention amid cuts to other student-facing positions.
overview: On April 7, 2025, the Superintendent defended retaining the Director of Mental/Behavioral Health, arguing the role provides essential, specialized expertise to meet student needs.
During the March 31, 2025 meeting, board members debated eliminating the Director of Mental and Behavioral Health position to fund the restoration of other staff roles.
On December 9, 2024, the Director of Mental Health reported on proactive staff work and a partnership to apply for a $500,000 grant to enhance services.
The board discussed robust mental health staffing and plans to partner with a national organization for suicide prevention on October 15, 2024.
In response to a student suicide crisis, the Superintendent announced plans on September 9, 2024, to hire a new Director of Mental and Behavioral Health and implement universal screeners.
On April 8, 2024, a parent suggested that investing in preventative measures like Pre-K could be a more effective use of funds than creating a new mental health leadership position.

Board: Questioned the rationale for retaining director-level positions like Mental/Behavioral Health while cutting others and requested cost analyses for alternatives (April 2025).
Proposed eliminating the Director of Mental and Behavioral Health position to pay for restoring SEL teachers (March 2025).
Acknowledged the urgent student mental health crisis following student deaths (September 2024).
Administration: Superintendent Metheny defended the Director of Mental/Behavioral Health role as providing essential, specialized expertise (April 2025).
The Superintendent presented data on achievement gaps and student well-being to justify retaining the Director of Mental and Behavioral Health (March 2025).
In response to a crisis, the Superintendent outlined plans to hire a Director of Mental and Behavioral Health, implement screeners, and expand training (September 2024).
Staff: Voiced opposition to cutting student-facing positions while the administration appears 'top-heavy' (April 2025).
Citizens: Opposed cutting student-facing positions while the administration seems 'top-heavy' and expressed concerns about budget transparency (April 2025).
Described the situation as a public health emergency and urged the district to immediately consult with external experts on suicide postvention (September 2024).
A parent suggested investing in preventative measures like Pre-K would be more proactive than creating a new leadership role for mental health (April 2024).

Middle School Consolidation.current_status: The plan to consolidate the two middle schools into one building has been removed from consideration for the FY27 budget. The administration cited feasibility issues but is still exploring the concept for a future year.
overview: On February 4, 2026, the administration removed the middle school consolidation plan from the FY27 budget due to feasibility concerns, but noted it is still being explored for FY28.

Administration: The timeline for FY27 was not feasible due to external dependencies like permitting and traffic studies.
The concept is still being explored for a future year, possibly FY28.

School Calendar 2026-2027.current_status: The first reading of the 2026-2027 school calendar has been postponed. The board is negotiating with the service employees' union regarding the impact of a proposed additional school day.
overview: On January 12, 2026, the board voted to postpone the first reading of the 2026-2027 school calendar to negotiate with the service employees' union.

Board: Voted to postpone the calendar's first reading to allow for union negotiations.
Staff: The service employees' union requires negotiations over the impact of an additional school day.

SPHS Athletic Field Referendum.current_status: The district is weighing the tax implications of natural grass versus synthetic turf for the proposed SPHS athletic field referendum. Public input has been received on the options while the project moves forward.
overview: On October 6, 2025, the Athletic Director presented the estimated first-year tax impact for both the natural grass and synthetic turf options for the high school athletic field referendum.

Administration: Athletic Director Todd Livingston presented the estimated tax impacts for both the natural grass and synthetic turf options.
Citizens: Some members of the public expressed support for the overall project but advocated for the natural grass option due to environmental and cost concerns with synthetic turf.

overview: On June 8, 2026, the board unanimously approved the new Educational Equity Policy.

Administration: The district's equity committee developed the policy to guide data review and address inequities.

SPMS Athletic Field Referendum.current_status: The board has approved revised wording for the upcoming municipal referendum on the SPMS athletic field. The changes are intended to clarify the choice between a natural grass field and a synthetic turf field for voters.
overview: On August 18, 2025, the board approved revised wording for the municipal referendum to clarify the choice between a natural grass field and a synthetic turf field.

Board: Voted to approve revised referendum wording to prevent voter confusion.

Board Leadership Change.current_status: Following the resignation of the previous vice chair, the board unanimously elected Member Smith to the position. Tandy Ratliff remains the Board Chair.
overview: On April 13, 2026, the board unanimously elected Member Smith as the new Vice Chair following the resignation of Adrian Dowling.
On August 18, 2025, the board elected Ms. DeAngelis as Vice Chair in a 4-2 vote, and Chair Tandy Ratliff announced she would not seek re-election at the end of her term.
On July 14, 2025, the board unanimously elected Tandy Ratliff as the new Board Chair.

Board: Members unanimously elected Smith as Vice Chair in April 2026.
Discussion in August 2025 centered on leadership precedent and the need for stability, leading to a 4-2 vote for Ms. DeAngelis as Vice Chair.
In July 2025, members unanimously elected Tandy Ratliff as Chair, praising her temperament and experience during a time of transition.

SPESPA Grievance.current_status: The Board of Education has unanimously denied a grievance from the South Portland Educational Support Staff Professionals Association (SPESPA). This decision was made following an Executive Session on January 8, 2025.
overview: On January 8, 2025, the board unanimously voted to deny a grievance from the South Portland Educational Support Staff Professionals Association (SPESPA) following an Executive Session.

Board: Unanimously voted to deny the SPESPA grievance.
Staff: The South Portland Educational Support Staff Professionals Association (SPESPA) filed a grievance that was ultimately denied.

Middle School Administration.current_status: A proposal to eliminate one of three assistant principal positions at South Portland Middle School was reversed. The position will be retained after staff and administrators argued it was essential for school operations.
overview: On March 24, 2025, the board reversed its initial support for a proposal to eliminate an assistant principal position at South Portland Middle School to save $141,000.

Board: Initially supported the elimination of the position but reversed the decision after hearing testimony.
Administration: Argued that running a split-grade school with two start times is untenable without adequate leadership.
Staff: Passionately argued that the school is untenable without the current number of administrators.

overview: On November 12, 2024, the board unanimously ratified a new three-year contract with the South Portland School District Service Employees Association.

Administration: The superintendent praised the collaborative and professional negotiation process.

Tobacco-Free Schools Policy.current_status: The board has given final approval to the Tobacco-Free Schools Policy. The policy is now officially adopted by the district.
overview: On January 8, 2024, the board gave final approval to the policy concerning tobacco-free schools as part of a larger consent agenda.

Board: The board unanimously approved the final policy.

Special Education.current_status: The board has received an overview of the Instructional Support department, which serves 649 students with disabilities. Public comment has been strongly supportive of the department and its programs.

During the March 25, 2024 meeting, citizens spoke in strong support of the Special Education department, sharing personal stories about the positive impact of programs like ELO.

Citizens: Spoke in strong support of the Special Education department, sharing personal stories of its positive impact.
Urged the board to maintain the ELO program and its coordinator, citing a graduate's success in finding a career path through the program.
